newsitem.title: ITALY: Occasional wifebeating OK, Italian court rules.
newsitem.headline: Occasional wifebeating OK, Italian court rules.

text.p: Italy's highest appeal court ruled on Wednesday that it is not a crime to beat your wife -- occasionally.

A jealous Sicilian husband whose "occasional episodes" of wife-beating were "interspersed with moments of harmony between the couple," should not have been sentenced to eight months in jail, the Court of Cassation ruled.
The verdict sparked howls of protest. "This case risks setting us back years," said Tina Lagostena Bassi, a member of parliament and former lawyer in domestic violence cases.
The husband in the case, whose name was not disclosed by court officials, said he did not strike his wife habitually, only from time to time, when he was jealous.
On one occasion she needed hospital treatment.

Sending the case back to a lower court in Palermo, the Court of Cassation said the case did not amount to domestic violence, which it defined as "a series of acts harming the physical integrity or liberty or dignity of the passive subject, who suffers a conduct of systematic and deliberate overpowering".
"To ask the victim to demonstrate the continuity of abuse and the intentional crushing of their personality is diabolical," said Bassi.
